content.text: Here are 2 worked examples of this kind of task, each with its map and a correct step-by-step solution. After them comes a new task with its own map. Solve the new task.

Worked example 1 (map above):

This is a topographic map of a real place (Bear Mountain, New York), drawn in the style of a USGS 7.5-minute quadrangle. The contour interval is 20 meters, index contours (heavy brown lines, some labeled) are every 100 meters, and elevations are in meters. Rescue carry: a stretcher team carries a casualty along the Aspen Trail (solid magenta line) from the magenta square S to the magenta square E. To pace the carry, the team leader logs every contour line the trail crosses. How many contour lines (index contours included) does the trail cross between S and E? Neither square stands on a contour line, so count only the crossings between the two squares. If the trail crosses the same contour line more than once, count every crossing. Answer with a whole number, for example 7.

Worked solution:
Trace the trail from S to E with a finger and note every contour line it crosses, in order: 60, 80, 100, 120, 140, 160, 160, 140, 120, 100, 80, 60 m. That is 6 crossings going uphill and 6 going downhill, 12 crossings in total. 2 of them are index contours (the heavy 100 m line crossed 2 times), and they count too (leaving them out would give 10).
FINAL ANSWER: 12

This is a topographic map of a real place (Breakneck Ridge, New York), drawn in the style of a USGS 7.5-minute quadrangle. The contour interval is 20 meters, index contours (heavy brown lines, some labeled) are every 100 meters, and elevations are in meters. Rescue carry: a stretcher team carries a casualty along the Summit Trail (solid magenta line) from the magenta square S to the magenta square E. To pace the carry, the team leader logs every contour line the trail crosses. How many contour lines (index contours included) does the trail cross between S and E? Neither square stands on a contour line, so count only the crossings between the two squares. If the trail crosses the same contour line more than once, count every crossing. Answer with a whole number, for example 7.

Worked solution:
Trace the trail from S to E with a finger and note every contour line it crosses, in order: 220, 200, 180, 160, 140, 120, 100, 80, 60, 40, 20 m. That is 0 crossings going uphill and 11 going downhill, 11 crossings in total. 2 of them are index contours (the heavy 200 m line and 100 m line), and they count too (leaving them out would give 9).
FINAL ANSWER: 11

New task (map above):

This is a topographic map of a real place (Mount Tamalpais, California), drawn in the style of a USGS 7.5-minute quadrangle. The contour interval is 20 meters, index contours (heavy brown lines, some labeled) are every 100 meters, and elevations are in meters. Rescue carry: a stretcher team carries a casualty along the Summit Trail (solid magenta line) from the magenta square S to the magenta square E. To pace the carry, the team leader logs every contour line the trail crosses. How many contour lines (index contours included) does the trail cross between S and E? Neither square stands on a contour line, so count only the crossings between the two squares. If the trail crosses the same contour line more than once, count every crossing. Answer with a whole number, for example 7.

Think step by step. Then end your reply with one final line in exactly this form:
FINAL ANSWER: <your answer>
